overview: This chapter follows the designed landscapes and museum ambitions associated with Prussia in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. It focuses on architects, craftspeople and the institutions that organized their work.

items.text: Frederick II commissioned Sanssouci between 1745 and 1747. The palace later hosted the French writer Voltaire.
In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, Potsdam's parks combined architecture with landscape gardening. Builders, painters, sculptors and gardeners contributed to the ensemble.
During the nineteenth century, Peter Joseph Lenne planned changes to the Havel landscape around Potsdam. Designed parkland linked water, buildings and views.
The Museum Island project in Berlin began in the nineteenth century. It treated museum architecture and the display of art and archaeology as a connected public undertaking.

sources.title: UNESCO, Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin
